{{Short description|Special tangential structure}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Spin<sup>h</sup> structure}}

In [[spin geometry]], a '''spin<sup>h</sup> structure''' (or '''quaternionic spin structure''') is a generalization of a [[spin structure]]. In mathematics, these are used to describe [[Spinor bundle|spinor bundles]] and [[Spinor|spinors]], which in physics are used to describe [[Spin (physics)|spin]], an intrinsic [[angular momentum]] of [[Particle|particles]] after which they have been named. Since spin<sup>h</sup> structures also exist under weakened conditions, which might not allow spin structures, they provide a suitable alternative for such situations. [[Orientability|Orientable]] manifolds with spin<sup>h</sup> structures are called '''spin<sup>h</sup> manifolds'''.<ref>Hu 2023, Def. 4.3</ref> H stands for the [[Quaternion|quaternions]], which are denoted <math>\mathbb{H}</math> and appear in the definition of the underlying [[Spinh group|spin<sup>h</sup> group]].

== Definition ==
Let <math>M</math> be a <math>n</math>-dimensional [[orientable manifold]]. Its [[tangent bundle]] <math>TM</math> is described by a classifying map <math>M\rightarrow\operatorname{BSO}(n)</math> into the [[Classifying space for SO(n)|classifying space]] <math>\operatorname{BSO}(n)</math> of the [[special orthogonal group]] <math>\operatorname{SO}(n)</math>. It can factor over the map <math>\operatorname{BSpin}^\mathrm{h}(n)\rightarrow\operatorname{BSO}(n)</math> induced by the canonical projection <math>\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{h}(n)\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{SO}(n)</math> on [[Classifying space|classifying spaces]]. In this case, the classifying map lifts to a continuous map <math>M\rightarrow\operatorname{BSpin}^\mathrm{h}(n)</math> into the classifying space <math>\operatorname{BSpin}^\mathrm{h}(n)</math> of the [[Spinh group|spin<sup>h</sup> group]] <math>\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{h}(n)</math>. Its [[homotopy]] class is called ''spin<sup>h</sup> structure''.<ref>Albanese & Milivojević 2021, Definition 3.1</ref>

Assume <math>M</math> has a spin<sup>h</sup> structure. Let then <math>\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{h}(M)</math> denote the set of spin<sup>h</sup> structures on <math>M</math>. The first symplectic group [[Principal U(1)-bundle|<math>\operatorname{Sp}(1)</math>]] is the second factor of the spin<sup>h</sup> group and using its [[Classifying space for SU(n)|classifying space]] [[Principal U(1)-bundle|<math>\operatorname{BSp}(1)
\cong\operatorname{BSU}(2)</math>]], which is the infinite [[quaternionic projective space]] [[Principal U(1)-bundle|<math>\mathbb{H}P^\infty</math>]] and through its [[Postnikov tower]] projects onto the [[Eilenberg–MacLane space]] <math>K(\mathbb{Z},4)</math>, there is a map:{{Citation needed|date=March 2025}}

: <math>\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{h}(M)
\cong[M,\operatorname{BSp}(1)]
\cong[M,\mathbb{H}P^\infty]
\rightarrow[M,K(\mathbb{Z},4)]
\cong H^4(M,\mathbb{Z}).</math>

The former isomorphism follows from the [[Puppe sequence]] for the fibration <math>\mathbb{H}P^\infty\hookrightarrow\operatorname{BSpin}^\mathrm{h}(n)\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{BSO}(n)</math> (when applying [[Principal U(1)-bundle|<math>[M,-]</math>]]).<ref>Albanese & Milivojević 2021, p. 5</ref> Although this map is not a bijection in general, it is in special cases, for example for a [[4-manifold]] <math>M</math>.

Due to the canonical projection <math>\operatorname{BSpin}^\mathrm{h}(n)\rightarrow\operatorname{SU}(2)/\mathbb{Z}_2
\cong\operatorname{SO}(3)</math>, every spin<sup>h</sup> structure induces a principal <math>\operatorname{SO}(3)</math>-bundle or equivalently a orientable real vector bundle of third rank.{{Citation needed|date=March 2025}}

== Properties ==

* Every spin and even every [[Spinc structure|spin<sup>c</sup> structure]] induces a spin<sup>h</sup> structure. Reverse implications don't hold as the [[complex projective plane]] <math>\mathbb{C}P^2</math> and the [[Wu manifold]] <math>\operatorname{SU}(3)/\operatorname{SO}(3)</math> show.<ref>Lawson 2023, p. 3</ref>
* If an orientable manifold <math>M</math> has a spin<sup>h</sup> structure, then its fifth integral Stiefel–Whitney class <math>W_5(M)
\in H^5(M,\mathbb{Z})</math> vanishes, hence is the image of the fourth ordinary Stiefel–Whitney class <math>w_4(M)
\in H^4(M,\mathbb{Z})</math> under the canonical map <math>H^4(M,\mathbb{Z}_2)\rightarrow H^4(M,\mathbb{Z})</math>.
* Every compact orientable smooth manifold with seven or less dimensions has a spin<sup>h</sup> structure.<ref>Albanese & Milivojević 2021, Theorem 1.4.</ref>
* In eight dimensions, there are infinitely many [[Homotopy type|homotopy types]] of [[Closed manifold|closed]] [[Simply connected space|simply connected]] manifolds without spin<sup>h</sup> structure.<ref>Albanese & Milivojević 2021, Theorem 1.5.</ref>
* For a [[Compact space|compact]] spin<sup>h</sup> manifold <math>M</math> of even dimension with either vanishing fourth [[Betti number]] <math>b_4(M)=\dim H^4(M,\mathbb{R})</math> or the first [[Pontryagin class|Pontrjagin class]] <math>p_1(E)\in H^4(M,\mathbb{Z})</math> of its canonical principal <math>\operatorname{SO}(3)</math>-bundle <math>E\twoheadrightarrow M</math> being torsion, twice its [[Â genus]] <math>2\widehat{A}(M)</math> is integer.<ref>Bär 1999, page 18</ref>

The following properties hold more generally for the lift on the Lie group <math>
\operatorname{Spin}^k(n)
:=\left(
\operatorname{Spin}(n)\times\operatorname{Spin}(k)
\right)/\mathbb{Z}_2
</math>, with the particular case <math>k=3</math> giving:

* If <math>M\times N</math> is a spin<sup>h</sup> manifold, then <math>M</math> and <math>N</math> are spin<sup>h</sup> manifolds.<ref name=":6">Albanese & Milivojević 2021, Proposition 3.6.</ref>
* If <math>M</math> is a spin manifold, then <math>M\times N</math> is a spin<sup>h</sup> manifold iff <math>N</math> is a spin<sup>h</sup> manifold.<ref name=":6" />
* If <math>M</math> and <math>N</math> are spin<sup>h</sup> manifolds of same dimension, then their [[connected sum]] <math>M\# N</math> is a spin<sup>h</sup> manifold.<ref name=":92">Albanese & Milivojević 2021, Proposition 3.7.</ref>
* The following conditions are equivalent:<ref name=":102">Albanese & Milivojević 2021, Proposition 3.2.</ref>
** <math>M</math> is a spin<sup>h</sup> manifold.
** There is a real vector bundle <math>E\twoheadrightarrow M</math> of third rank, so that <math>TM\oplus E</math> has a spin structure or equivalently <math>w_2(TM\oplus E)
=0</math>.
** <math>M</math> can be immersed in a spin manifold with three dimensions more.
** <math>M</math> can be embedded in a spin manifold with three dimensions more.

== Cohomology of infinite classifying space ==
The [[cohomology ring]] of the infinite classifying space <math>\operatorname{BSpin}^\mathrm{h}
:=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\operatorname{BSpin}^\mathrm{h}(n)</math> with coefficients in <math>\mathbb{Z}_2</math> can be expressed using [[Steenrod square|Steenrod squares]] and [[Wu class|Wu classes]]:<ref>Lawson 2023, p. 8</ref><ref>Hu 2023, Thrm. 4.29</ref>
: <math>H^*(\operatorname{BSpin}^\mathrm{h},\mathbb{Z}_2)
\cong H^*(\operatorname{BSO},\mathbb{Z}_2)/(\operatorname{Sq}^1\nu_{2^r},r\geq 2).</math>
